evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Fields to enter are explicitly named and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Mechanism (URL) and purpose are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Input method and artifact are explicitly specified.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: ‘Items we try to estimate this session’ is clear in context.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Action and target are specific and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: The artifact and intent are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item is concrete and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Delete action and effect (not estimate it) are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: 'Show all estimates immediately' describes a clear moderator action and intent.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: ‘Average’ is ambiguous (mean, median, mode) and leads to materially different outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Condition and automatic fill behavior are explicitly stated.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: The target (agreed-upon estimate) is clear in context of the workflow.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Intent and scope (earlier in the session) are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Import source is specified and unambiguous at the story level.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Action and source are concrete and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is a clear request without vague terms.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Transcript artifact and intent are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Output format (HTML) and artifact (transcript) are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Output format (CSV) and artifact are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: The desired effect (no longer stored) is understandable as permanent removal in context.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation fields are explicitly listed.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Credentials required for login are explicitly specified.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: While broad, this is a common, concrete user action and not inherently vague in this backlog context.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Desired effect (no longer stored) is clear in context of account deletion.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Requirement explicitly names the timezone behavior desired.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Delivery method (email) and artifact (password reminder) are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Options are explicitly enumerated, removing ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Numeric limit is explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Join mechanism and fields are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: The item to be estimated is clearly the content shown.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope (this session) and artifact (items) are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: The visibility requirement is explicit about who gave an estimate and immediate notification.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Condition and timing are explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: The permitted window for changes is explicitly defined.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Requested data (prior estimates for the story) is explicitly specified.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Visibility requirement is explicit about round and mapping of estimators to estimates.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and visibility are explicit.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reset condition and duration are explicitly stated.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Navigation and scope are concrete and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Behavior (card order consistency) is explicitly defined.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Condition for changing estimate is explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Although 'small' is relative, the intended UI element and placement are clear and not likely to cause materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards to comply with are explicitly named and concrete.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Request for definitions is explicit and not vague.

evaluations.evidence: so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: ‘As fast as possible’ is vague and permits materially different performance targets/implementations.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Target browsers and versions are explicitly listed.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Phrase ‘where possible’ is vague and allows materially different interpretations of compliance scope.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: ‘Quickly’ is undefined and can lead to materially different performance targets.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Requirement (Unicode support) is concrete and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Terms ‘sensible’ and ‘predictable’ are subjective and can be interpreted materially differently.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: ‘Nice’ is subjective and permits materially different UI/UX interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: ‘Non-identifiable’ is ambiguous (degree and method of anonymization not specified) and can lead to materially different privacy implementations.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: ‘Some metrics’ is underspecified and allows materially different interpretations of which metrics are required.
